messages:
john.doe: Heads-up — paying customer 'AcmeMobile' opened a high-sev ticket: all API requests started returning 401 around 09:23 UTC after a scheduled key rotation. They say they updated their side with the new key but still getting auth failures. Ticket ID #CM-8421.

maria.su: ack. I asked for the exact error payload and example curl. They shared: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key revoked or unknown"}
```

kevin_oncall: :rotating_light: tagging eng-oncall. Did we do an automated rotation job for AcmeMobile today?

tara_security: We ran scheduled rotation for org-acmemobile at 09:20 UTC (cron: rotate-keys.sh). Vault recorded a rotation event: key-id 7f4c3 rotated -> 9a2b1. I'll paste audit snippet: 
```
type=rotate, entity=org:acmemobile, old_key=7f4c3, new_key=9a2b1, user=svc-rotator, status=success
```

alex_infra: Rotation job succeeded from the rotator side. But I see a subsequent revoke for 7f4c3 at 09:21 with reason=manual_revocation by svc-rotator. That should be fine — old key revoked after grace window. Did customer pull new secret from Vault or from their CI before revoke?

maria.su: Customer claims they updated the key; I asked for the first 8 chars of the key they set in their env (masked) and they replied 7f4c3... which matches the old key. So they're still using the old key.

kevin_oncall: OK that explains 401. Why would customer still have old value after rotation? Two likely causes: (1) they cached the env var in a long-lived process and didn't restart, or (2) they read the key from our legacy KMS path that wasn't updated. Ask them to run a quick check: `echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY | head -c 8` and also show us their deployment restart logs.

maria.su: Sent steps. Customer responded: we pulled new key from Vault GUI but our helm chart mounts secrets as static files — we thought the chart automatically refreshes but it doesn't. They will restart the pods.

tara_security: Quick note for internal docs: when rotating keys we have a default 60s revocation grace window for orgs on Dedicated, 300s for Hosted. For future: ensure rotation job sets final revoke after grace window only once confirmation webhook is received from secret-sync-controller. Looks like their helm-based deployment never hit the webhook.

alex_infra: I also checked logs on our secret-sync-controller; there was a 5xx at 09:19 to the customer's namespace webhook (timeout). It retried but the last attempt timed out and we proceeded to revoke after grace. I filed infra ticket INF-590 to increase retry/observability.

maria.su: Customer restarted pods at 09:35 and confirms now receiving 200s. But they reported recurring confusion: their CI saved the key in plaintext in GitLab CI env with scope limited to project, and they accidentally rotated the wrong secret once. They asked for best practices for rotation/secret storage.

kevin_oncall: Can we provide a short runbook: how to rotate safely + fallback? Also include commands for verifying permissions, scope, and logs. Draft: 
- Always pull new key and verify first 8 chars before revocation
- Restart consumers or use secret refresh (k8s CSI driver or HashiVault injector)
- Keep a short fallback window & replicate new key to an alternate secret path if secretsync fails
- Use service accounts with minimal scopes for automated rotation jobs

tara_security: Add specifics: use KMS/HSM-managed keys for at-rest encryption, store API key IDs in metadata so you can verify which key is active, and prefer Vault with dynamic secrets for limited TTL. Also: avoid saving plaintext tokens in repo or CI variables without masking. Provide example policy: 
```
path "secret/data/acme/*" {
  capabilities = ["read", "list"]
  allowed_entities = ["svc-deployer", "team-acme"]
}
```

alex_infra: For support we should include quick repro checks: 
1) GET /v1/account/keys (admin) -> see active key id and created_at
2) Vault audit logs: filter by entity=org:acmemobile and event=rotate/revoke
3) Check sync controller logs: `kubectl logs -n secrets system-secret-sync -l app=secret-sync`

maria.su: I posted those steps to the customer and included a short snippet to restart pods gracefully: `kubectl rollout restart deployment -n acme-mobile` and suggested enabling the Vault injector (link). They thanked us.

kevin_oncall: Closing loop: root cause = secret-sync controller timeout + customer using static mount (no refresh) -> old key stayed in runtime -> revocation caused 401s. Action items: 
- INF-590: increase retry logic on secret-sync-controller (alex)
- DOC-457: add rotation runbook for support (maria)
- SEC-312: update default grace window behavior and webhook confirmation before final revoke (tara)

maria.su: I'll update ticket CM-8421 with resolution notes and recommend customer adopt CSI/Vault injector + rotate in a canary namespace first. Marking customer follow-up: offer a migration call.

incident-bot: Incident resolved by support. Resolution: keys rotated successfully; issue caused by local secret refresh lag. Severity: P2.

kevin_oncall: Thanks everyone. Leaving a short snippet for internal KB: 
```
# quick-check for 401 after rotation
# 1) confirm env value on host/pod: echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY | head -c 8
# 2) confirm active key id from API (admin): curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/account/keys
# 3) check Vault audit: vault audit list | grep rotate | grep acmemobile
# 4) check secret-sync-controller logs and webhook delivery
```

maria.su: closing thread, will attach KB link once DOC-457 is done. :lock:
